assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength idea with Sr/Yb lattice spectroscopy to reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, which is about two orders better than the caesium standard. It is original, conceptually clean and already opens gravitational redshift tests at the millimetre scale, searches for varying constants and the route to a redefined second. As an atomic physicist I regard the underlying atomic structure and systematic-shift control as exemplary precision work.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated the first Sr lattice clock; Ye's group drove the record accuracy and stability and the comparisons and applications. Two laureates fit the supplied credit cleanly. Others (e.g. Lemonde, Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley) are not in the supplied credit and I cannot expand it. Hall and Haensch were honoured in 2005 for the frequency comb, which is a distinct enabling invention.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent groups worldwide operate lattice clocks, results are reproduced and compared across continents, and the redefinition of the second is under active discussion. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the committee would view clocks as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 comb prize.
Relative weight of Katori's scheme versus Ye's accuracy demonstration is a judgment I cannot settle from the supplied text.
I have not independently verified the latest clock uncertainty figures.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction and observation of the quantum spin Hall state and topological insulators opened a new classification of band matter, with protected edge and surface states, and has influenced spintronics, cold-atom analogues and topological photonics. It is conceptually original and widely taught.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction of the Z2 quantum spin Hall effect; Molenkamp's group, following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal and König et al., observed the effect in HgTe. Hasan's 3D topological insulator work is also credited, but with a three-person cap, Kane, Mele and Molenkamp give the most coherent theory-plus-experiment configuration. BHZ and Zhang are not in the supplied credit, so a fair allocation is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Mature: two decades of independent confirmation (HgTe, Bi-Sb, Bi2Se3, ARPES and transport), and the topological band theory framework is stable. Timely, with the 2016 prize covering topological phase transitions in a different sense.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 topological-matter prize needs weighing.
Credit split between 2D and 3D topological insulators, and the missing BHZ proposal, remain unresolved.
Practical applications are still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are direct, striking tests of strong-field gravity and accretion physics, achieved through very-long-baseline interferometry at 1.3 mm. The result is clear to scientists and the public alike and rests on a major technical achievement.
assessment.attribution: The credit mixes the original shadow concept and imaging proposal (Falcke), accretion-flow theory (Narayan) and the instrumental and VLBI realization (Doeleman). The EHT is a collaboration of hundreds, which complicates a three-person allocation; this is the main weakness. The supplied names are the only ones available to me.
assessment.maturity: Reasonably mature: two independent sources, a multi-year polarization series and consistency with general relativity. Interpretation of parameters such as spin is still model dependent, so some caution is warranted.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration attribution makes a three-person configuration contestable.
Model-dependent interpretation of accretion and spin.
Overlap with the 2020 black-hole prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The recollision (three-step) picture and the strong-field quantum theory of high-harmonic generation explain the mechanism that underlies attosecond pulse generation, and provided the framework for attosecond spectroscopy. It is original, simple and quantitatively successful.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's semiclassical model and Lewenstein et al.'s quantum theory are the decisive contributions; both names are supplied. L'Huillier, Agostini and Krausz were awarded in 2023 for attosecond light-pulse generation, so credit here is adjacent to an already recognized discovery. I must disclose that I have a long-standing scientific collaboration with Anne L'Huillier and work in attosecond theory, so I treat my own ranking with care and would not push this above clean atomic or condensed-matter candidates.
assessment.maturity: Mature: confirmed over three decades by many experiments and used across attosecond science. However, recognition may look partly redundant after 2023.
uncertainties: Possible overlap with the 2023 prize makes novelty of recognition debatable.
Disclosed collaboration with L'Huillier and attosecond community; I do not claim impartiality about this field.
Whether Corkum alone would better represent the idea.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought cavity-QED strong coupling into superconducting circuits and underlies readout, gates and coupling of superconducting qubits. It is a foundational platform for quantum technology and tests of light-matter interaction in new regimes.
assessment.attribution: Blais et al. provided the theory proposal, and Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues provided the first strong-coupling demonstration in 2004. These three names support a reasonable configuration, although Yale and ETH groups and others (e.g. Devoret, Nakamura) contributed in related ways and are not in this credit.
assessment.maturity: Mature as a platform, with broad independent implementation. However, the 2025 prize on macroscopic circuit quantum behaviour makes a second superconducting-circuit award soon after less likely, in my view.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2025 prize topic.
Overlap of credit with other circuit-qubit pioneers who are not listed.
Whether the discovery or the technology is the prize-relevant object.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realize Hubbard models with tunable parameters and allow direct observation of the Mott insulator and many-body dynamics, a long-standing aim of quantum simulation. This is original and has changed many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Five names are supplied; I can only name three. Zoller (with Jaksch and Cirac) proposed the Bose-Hubbard realization; Greiner and Bloch observed the superfluid to Mott transition and developed quantum-gas microscopy; Esslinger realized the Fermi-Hubbard case. Choosing three omits genuinely decisive contributors, so allocation is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Fairly mature for bosons and fermions, though the key physics questions (e.g. d-wave in the Fermi-Hubbard model) remain open, so the full scientific payoff is not yet established.
uncertainties: Five credited people against a three-laureate limit.
Hubbard-model physics at low temperatures is still not fully reached.
Overlap with the 2001 Bose-Einstein condensation prize and the 1997 cooling prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry provides inertial sensing, measurements of gravity and of the fine-structure constant, and tests of the equivalence principle at high precision. It is a natural extension of Ramsey and Chu-type work, and a good example of matter-wave physics applied to metrology.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard demonstrated early atom interferometers, Bordé developed the theoretical and Ramsey-Bordé interferometer framework, and Kasevich built the high-performance gravimeters and gradiometers. Müller is also credited but the three-person limit forces a choice; this is not clearly resolved. Chu's 1997 prize on laser cooling touched related techniques.
assessment.maturity: Mature technically, with commercial gravimeters and many independent groups, although a single decisive fundamental discovery is harder to point to.
uncertainties: Diffuse credit across four people and several groups.
Whether this is an invention or a discovery in the prize sense.
Overlap with earlier laser-cooling prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene, with a theoretical flat-band prediction and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity, created the moire materials field and a very active area of correlated-electron physics. It is highly original and influential.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction of the magic angle and flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. This is a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration. The Cao et al. first author is not in the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Relatively young: central results have been reproduced across groups, but the mechanism of superconductivity is debated and the field is still developing, so recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Superconducting pairing mechanism is unsettled.
Possibly premature relative to the older candidates on my list.
This is outside my own field, so I rely on general knowledge and have not verified details.
